3. The suit was filed stating, inter alia, that the land in suit belong to Karunakanta Roy and others and they settled the land in suit to Amir Ali Kazi and his brother sayed Kazi in 1342 B.S. and that on the death of the aforesaid 2 settlement holders their heirs became owner of the land in suit, that R.S. record was prepared in the name of Zaminder and thereupon Amir Ali Kazi filed Miscellaneous case under section 143 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act in the office of the Sub-Division Manager and Revenue Officer Acquired Estate, Bogra on December 24, 1966 and thereupon record of right was correctly prepared by the order of January 30, 1967, that some time after the order allowing the correction of the record Amir Ali Kazi died and that the heirs of All were not aware of the order for correction of the record, that in the first part of June 1984 plaintiff No.1 came to know about the order for correction of the record and thereupon obtained the certified copy on June 14. 1984, that MRR khatian having not been prepared in the name of the predecessor of the plaintiffs some greedy persons of the locality tried to grab the property in suit, that the kabala in the name of the defendant No.2 is forged, that plaintiffs are in possession of the pond and rearing fish and that also possessing the bank of the tank by cultivating vegetable, that as the wrong record of right has given rise to serious complications in the enjoyment of the property by the plaintiffs and also clouded title of the plaintiffs they are constrained to file the suit. 

 4. The suit was contested by defendant Nos. 1 and 2 as well as by the defendant Nos.2 I - 25 by filing separate written statements. The case of the defendant No.1 was that suit was barred by limitation and that the suit was not maintainable because of the provision of section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, that the land in suit belonged to landlord lswar and others and accordingly MRR record was prepared and published in their names, that since the time of Zaminder the pond in question is used by the people of the locality, that recorded tenants having had left for India the property vested in the Government as vested property and that Government is possessing the land by leasing out the same to different persons. 

 5. It was the case of the defendant Nos.21-25 that after the whole sale acquisition of the rent receiving interest the property as excess land of the Zaminder vested in the Government and that people of the locality enjoying the pond under the Government by rearing fish, that plaintiffs or the defendant No.2 have no possession and as such the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 9. The learned Deputy Attorney General submits that as the trial Court on consideration of the evidence arrived at the finding that the Plaintiffs claim of the land on the basis of pattan is not true and that the plaintiffs failed to prove the Dakhilas in accordance with the law and that the Dakhilas were created for the purpose of the suit and that the sub-Divisional Manager of the government acquired Estate has no jurisdiction to correct the revenue record under section 143 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act but the Court of appeal below without adverting to the said findings of the trial Court set 'aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court and the judgment of the appellate Court being not a proper judgment of reversal High Court Division was in error in not interfering with the judgment of the Court of appeal below. that the trial Court having had held that the original and the admitted owners of the property in suit having left the country, the property vested in the Government and the High Court Division as failed to take into consideration the provision of Article 143(I)(e) of the Constitution and as such the High Court Division erred in not setting aside the judgment of the appellate Court and consequent thereupon in not setting aside the findings of the appellate Court that the Government did not produce evidence to establish that the property in suit is a vested property. that the finding of the trial Court as regard possession being based on evidence and that the reasoning given by the trial Court in rejecting the claim of the plaintiffs as regard their possession of the land in suit being backed by cogent, the High Court Division was in error in not setting aside the finding of the Court of appeal below with regard to question of possession of the land in suit. 

 12. In that state of the matter we are of the view the High Court 'Division was not in error in refusing to interfere with the judgment of the High Court Division.
